name: The Boogeyman, Not Voldemort
claim: The folk theory that parties stop naming an opposing president is backwards: the out-party names the sitting president about twice as often as his own party does — every year, both parties, 2013-2026 — and it tracks who holds the White House, not who holds Congress.

numbers.metric: sitting-president name-token rate per 1k words, out-party vs in-party
numbers.power_position: resolved to WHITE HOUSE control: 2013-14 Republicans held the House majority yet named Obama ~2.6x as the WH out-party

confounds_tested: both-halves gate -> PASSES (8/8 and 6/6), unlike S2.3/S1.10 which failed it
party-asymmetry -> resolved: it is WH-control (out-party) not chamber-minority; symmetric across both parties in both directions
reference dates -> president terms verified; chambers-control 118 potus corrected D (Biden)
split_result: holds in both halves and under both parties in each WH role
chart_spec: 14 years x2 lines (out-party vs in-party president-name rate), or the out/in ratio bar per year annotated with which president
receipts_note: receipts = statements naming the sitting president, member+date+url; abundant
republication_note: this is a CONFIRMED directional finding (refutes the pre-registered avoidance hypothesis); publishable as-is with the mention!=hostility label
neutrality_gate: null (symmetric: the effect holds identically for whichever party is out of the White House; the reversal, not a party, is the story)
